THOUSANDS SIGN PETITION, HUNDREDS REGISTER TO VOTE

Reading, MA - Thousands signed the petition and hundreds registered to vote at Mass Cann/NORML's 10th Annual Freedom Rally held this past Saturday on the Boston Common. The six hour Freedom Rally drew over 100,000 people over the course of the afternoon. For the seventh year in a row, the weather was ideal for one of the largest anti-war on marijuana protests in the world.

"The people of Boston should ask their Mayor and city councilors about the exorbitant cost of the police presence, which we estimate to have been well over 100 officers for at least eight hours. This was a peaceful event, as always, except for the police arrests of marijuana smokers. The one incident of concern to us is that someone brought a small gun to the rally.

It was found by police when booking a person arrested on marijuana charges, but for those charges no one would have ever known about the gun," said Mass Cann spokesperson, Attorney Steven Epstein. "Had our marijuana decrim proposal been in effect the officers would have cited persons, like giving them a traffic ticket, and the civil fines would have totaled $14,000.00," Epstein added.

Park Rangers and Parks and Recreation Department staff complemented organizers on their distribution of thousands of trash bags toward the end of the event. "It was an extraordinary social phenomenon, those in attendance were asked to help clean-up and they did. By nine o'clock the parade ground was as clean as when we arrived Friday afternoon," said Epstein.
